findings.description: `assertNoGitlink` checks `<common>/worktrees/<id>/index`, a file sessions can write, and codegraph only reads that same file later. Between the two, a session-side writer can add a gitlink over a `.git` the session already planted in its worktree. codegraph's git then enters the submodule and runs that repo's clean filter outside the sandbox.
findings.body:
**The gitlink check and codegraph read the index at different times.**

`assertNoGitlink` runs `ls-files --stage` against `GIT_DIR=<common>/worktrees/<id>`. `indexDirectory` then hands codegraph that same `GIT_DIR` through `indexEnv(git)`:

```ts
function assertNoGitlink(git: WorktreeGitEnv): void {
  const entries = runGit(git.GIT_WORK_TREE, ['ls-files', '--stage', '-z'], { env: { ...git } });
  const gitlink = entries.split('\0').find((entry) => entry.startsWith('160000 '));
  ...
}
...
  assertNoGitlink(git);
  ...
  execFileSync(binary, initialized ? ['index', directory, '--quiet'] : ['init', directory, '--yes'], {
    env: indexEnv(git),
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3971c3d71e16035627be27a37c8388bc2f7da682/src/core/codegraph.client.ts#L220-L255

Decision 101 says a session can write files in that admin dir: the sandbox write-protects neither pointer file there, and the ceilings paragraph assumes a session that rewrites an admin dir's `index`. So the index codegraph reads may not be the one pup checked. Killing the window on a respawn does not stop a sibling session or a process that outlived the window.

**What follows if a gitlink is in the index when codegraph's git reads it.** Decision 101 already describes it. A `.gitmodules` `ignore = none` outranks `diff.ignoreSubmodules=all`, and the submodule's child git clears the pins. If the session has also planted an untracked `lib/x/.git` that names a repo it built with `filter.x.clean`, that filter runs outside the sandbox with the operator's environment. Closing that path is the reason for this check.

This window is not listed under decision 101's *Ceilings*. It affects every `indexDirectory` caller whose worktree a session has already run in: the respawn, the fix round and the conductor.

**Suggested fix:** check a snapshot the session cannot change, and let codegraph read the same bytes.
1. Copy `<admin>/index` to a file pup owns (`mkdtemp`).
2. Run a pinned `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<copy> git update-index --no-split-index`, so a split index's `link` extension does not still read `$GIT_DIR/sharedindex.*`.
3. Run the `ls-files --stage` check against the copy.
4. Pass `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<copy>` in `indexEnv`.

If this window is meant to stay open, list it under decision 101's ceilings instead.

findings.description: Stale comments still say `worktree add` checks out files and runs the smudge filter (fix-round.service.ts L397-401, session-lifecycle.service.ts L195-196, git-diff.client.ts L653-654). Every add is now `--no-checkout`, so the smudge runs in `checkoutPinned`'s `read-tree -u`. Unresolved from the prior review.

The JSDoc of `dropUncheckedWorktree` (and of `dropUncheckedRound` in fix-round.service.ts L434-436) says it "Returns what it undid", but its catch branch returns a "could not remove" message. Say it returns the advice instead. Unresolved from the prior review.

Call-site `--no-checkout` comments still restate `checkoutPinned`'s JSDoc (session-lifecycle.service.ts L600-601, fix-round.service.ts L404-407), which docs/conventions/general.md §Comments treats as a duplicate. The launch copy also sits above the `rev-parse` line rather than the `worktree add` it describes.

The `measureBranch` comment ("What git reads of the pinned sha is read from the main checkout's repo, never through the checkout's admin dir…") restates the JSDoc on `CapabilityContext.measureSha` and on `nestedPackageDirs`. That is the seam-duplication case in docs/conventions/general.md §Comments; drop those two sentences.

When the prune keeps a locked admin dir, the fix round's advice (`rm -r .worktrees/<id>` then `git worktree prune`) cannot clear it, so the retry is refused again with the same advice. Mention `git worktree unlock` (or `git worktree remove -f -f`).

`checkoutPinned`'s `read-tree` and `refuseEscapingLinks`' pinned `ls-tree` (merge-gate.service.ts:454) have no `timeout`. A session that swaps a fifo in for `<admin>/HEAD` right after the add hangs the gate inside the merge lock. `committedPackageDirs` already passes `GATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`.

The new gitfile refusal says "Run it from the main checkout", but `repoRoot` already maps a linked worktree to the main repo. A `--separate-git-dir` clone or a submodule resolves repoPath to the git dir itself, so the operator who sees this advice is already in the main checkout and cannot act on it.

`dropUncheckedRound` repeats `dropUncheckedWorktree`'s rmSync / prune / admin-dir lstat undo and the same catch-and-rewrap of `WorktreeRepointedError` (session-lifecycle.service.ts L545-568, L604-613). A fix to the undo now has to be made in both. At two uses this is optional; a shared `removeAddedWorktree` in git-diff.client.ts would hold the common part.

The fix round builds its `WorktreeRepointedError` through the new `advice` parameter and then appends `NOT_STARTED` to `refusal.message`. The message is half constructed and half patched, so the class's "kept in its parts" design doesn't quite fit its second caller.

`prepareGraph(binary, repoPath, directory, pinned)` receives the work tree twice: `directory` is used only for the failure message, while indexing uses `pinned().GIT_WORK_TREE`, so callers must keep the two in sync by hand. Have `pinned` take `directory`, or note that they must agree.
The git PATH-shim setup is pasted inline in two new launch tests, while the matching fix-round tests in this PR use a `shimGit(shimCase)` helper. A local helper would remove the copy.

The same ~10-line `worktree add` commondir-rewriting PATH shim is pasted here and in merge-gate.test.ts:1962-1982, and the promisor-remote trap repo appears in both git-tree-client.test.ts:95-112 and merge-gate.test.ts:2663-2672. Shared fixtures would keep each attack recipe in one place.

The conductor's refresh path (`checkout --detach refs/heads/<target>`) still trusts the session-writable admin dir's `HEAD` and `index` (and a planted sparse-checkout). A session can therefore keep files out of the conductor's checkout and blind its graph. Refreshing with `checkoutPinned` (`read-tree --reset -u`), as the first cut does, would narrow this. The same was true on main.

Unpinned `git worktree prune` (here, fix-round L378, merge-gate.service.ts:531, conductor.service.ts:139) may follow a session-planted symlink at `<common>/worktrees/x -> ~/.ssh` and recursively delete its target outside the sandbox. lstat-refusing non-directory entries under `<common>/worktrees/` before any prune would close it. This rests on git internals recalled from memory.

`insertSession` still runs before `launchSession`, whose `verifiedWorktreeGitEnv` can throw. Nothing undoes the row, worktree or branch on that throw; the new undo covers only a `checkoutPinned` throw. Unresolved from the prior review.

process_issues.description: The review-validator for the codegraph.client.ts gitlink TOCTOU finding reported that a safety classifier cut off its first response partway through. Its CONFIRMED verdict rests on the code and decision-101 text it had read before the cutoff.

review-context and review-spec were not spawned. No spec/protocol/infra surface was touched, and no closing issue or --spec source exists (closingIssuesReferences is empty and no closing keywords were found).
